1.1: And it came to pass, when the king of the Chaldeans had taken the children of Israel captive, that the Lord spake unto Jeremiah, saying:
1.2: Jeremiah, my chosen, arise and go forth out of this city, thou and Baruch; for I will destroy it because of the multitude of the sins of them that dwell therein. For thy prayer is as a strong pillar in the midst of the city, and as a wall of adamant round about it. Now therefore arise ye, and go and depart, before the host of the Chaldeans come and compass the city.
1.3: And Jeremiah answered, saying: I beseech thee, my Lord, suffer thy servant to speak before thee.
1.4: And the Lord said unto him: Speak, my chosen Jeremiah.
1.5: And Jeremiah answered and said: O Lord of all, wilt thou deliver this chosen city into the hands of the Chaldeans, that the king with his people may boast and say, I have prevailed against the city of God?
1.6: Nay, my Lord; but if it please thee, destroy it with thine own hands.
1.7: And the Lord said unto Jeremiah: Because thou art my chosen, arise and go forth, thou and Baruch; for I will destroy it because of the sins of them that dwell therein. And neither the king nor his host shall be able to enter into the city, except I first open and enlarge the gates thereof.
1.8: Arise now, and go unto Baruch, and tell him this word; and when the sixth hour of the night is come, enter ye within the walls of the city, and I will shew you: for except I first destroy the city, they shall not be able to enter into it.
1.9: And when the Lord had spoken these things, he departed from Jeremiah.

2.1: And Jeremiah rent his garments, and cast ashes upon his head, and entered into the house of the sanctuary.
2.2: And Baruch saw Jeremiah [with] ashes strewn upon his head, and his garments rent; and he cried with a loud voice, saying: My father Jeremiah, what aileth thee? and what sin have the people committed? For when the people sinned, Jeremiah mourned, and cast ashes upon his head, and prayed for the people, that their iniquity might be forgiven them.
2.3: And Baruch asked him, saying: My father Jeremiah, what aileth thee, and what is become of the people?
2.4: And Jeremiah said unto him: Take heed that we rend not our garments, but let us rend our hearts; and let us put no water into the basins, that we may weep bitterly until we fill them with our tears: for from henceforth he will have no mercy on this people.
2.5: And Baruch said: My father Jeremiah, what aileth thee?
2.6: And Jeremiah said unto him: God will deliver the city into the hand of the king of the Chaldeans; for he shall lead the people captive in affliction.
2.7: And when Baruch heard all this, he rent his garments, and said: My father Jeremiah, who hath shewed thee this?
2.8: And Jeremiah said unto him: Abide with me until the sixth hour of the night, that thou mayest know that the word is true.
2.9: And they abode in the house of the sanctuary, weeping.

3.1: And when the sixth hour of the night was come, whereof the Lord had told Jeremiah, that he should go up with Baruch, they went up within the walls of the city, and abode watching.
3.2: And there was the sound of a trumpet, and angels came forth from heaven, holding torches of fire in their hands, and stood within the walls of the city.
3.3: And when Jeremiah and Baruch saw them, they wept, saying: Now we know that the word is true.
3.4: And Jeremiah besought the angels, saying: I beseech you all, destroy not the city, until I ask one word of the Lord;
3.5: and the Lord answered the angels, saying: Destroy not the city, until I speak with Jeremiah my chosen.
3.6: Then spake Jeremiah, saying: I beseech thee, my Lord, give me leave to speak with thee. And he said unto him: Speak, my chosen Jeremiah, whatsoever thou wilt.
3.7: And Jeremiah said unto him: Behold, now we know, my Lord, that thou wilt deliver the city into the hand of the enemy, and the people shall be carried away to Babylon. What wilt thou that I do with the holy vessels of our ministry, which thou hast committed unto us? and what wilt thou that I do concerning them?
3.8: And the Lord said unto him: Take them, and commit them to the earth, and to the house of the sanctuary, saying:
3.9: And thou, O earth, hear the voice of thy Creator, who formed thee in the abundance of waters, who sealed thee with seven seals: take again thy beauty, and guard the vessels of thy ministry until the coming of the Beloved.
3.10: And Jeremiah answered and said: I beseech thee, my Lord, shew me what I shall do for Abimelech the Ethiopian; for he hath done many kindnesses unto the people and unto thy servant Jeremiah: he was distinguished above all the men of the city, and he drew me out of the miry pit; and I would not that he should see the destruction and desolation of the city, lest he be grieved.
3.11: And the Lord said unto Jeremiah: Send him into the vineyard of Agrippa, by the mountain way; and I will hide him, until I bring the people again into the city;
3.12: and thou, Jeremiah, go with the people until ye come to the land of Babylon, and abide prophesying unto them, until I bring them into their city;
3.13: but leave thou Baruch here in Jerusalem.
3.14: And when the Lord had spoken all this unto Jeremiah, he departed from Jeremiah into heaven.
3.15: And Jeremiah and Baruch entered into the house of the sanctuary, and committed all the vessels of their ministry unto the earth, as the Lord had commanded them; and straightway the earth swallowed them, and they twain abode and wept.
3.16: And in the morning Jeremiah sent Abimelech, saying: Take a basket, and go by the mountain way into the vineyard of Agrippa, and bring a few figs for the sick of the people; for the favour of the Lord is upon thy head, and his glory. And he went as he commanded him.

4.1: And in the morning the host of the Chaldeans compassed the city; and a great angel blew the trumpet, saying: Enter ye, O host of the Chaldeans; behold, the gates are opened unto you.
4.2: Then the king entered with his army, and they took all the people captive.
4.3: And then Jeremiah took the keys of the house of the sanctuary, and went forth out of the city, and cast these keys before the sun, saying: Unto thee I speak, O sun: take the keys of the house of God, and keep them until the day wherein the Lord shall require them of thee; for we were not found worthy to keep them, for we have been found unfaithful in our sins.
4.4: And while Jeremiah was yet weeping for the people, they brought him forth and dragged him, and led him away with the people unto Babylon.
4.5: But Baruch took ashes and cast them upon his head, and abode and wailed this wailing, saying:
4.6: Wherefore is Jerusalem made desolate? but for the sin of the beloved people was she delivered into the hand of her enemies, for our sins and for the sins of the people;
4.7: but let not the sinners boast, neither let them say: We were able to take the city of God by our might; it was not by your strength that ye prevailed against her, but for our sins was she delivered unto you;
4.8: and our God will have mercy upon us, and bring us again into our city; but as for you, there shall be no life. Blessed are our fathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob; for they departed out of this world, and saw not the destruction of this city.
4.9: And after he had spoken this, he went forth weeping, and said: I mourn for thee, O Jerusalem. And he went out of the city, and abode in a tomb; and the angels came unto him, and shewed him concerning all things.

5.1: And Abimelech took the figs at the time of midday, as Jeremiah had sent him; and he found a shady tree, and abode and rested, to take a little rest; and he leaned his head upon the basket of figs, and slept sixty and six years, and awoke not from his sleep.
5.2: And after a time he arose and awoke from his sleep, and said: I have slept sweetly a little while; for my head is heavy, and I have not had my fill of sleep.
5.3: And he uncovered that basket of figs, and found the figs fresh, and their milk dripping.
5.4: And he desired to sleep again, for his head was heavy, and he was not sated with slumber; and he said: I fear lest I sleep and be late, lest my father Jeremiah rebuke me; for he sent me early in the morning. And now I will arise and go; for is there not heat, is there not toil, every day?
5.5: And he arose, and took up the basket of his figs, and entered into the city Jerusalem; and he knew not the city, nor his house. And he said: Blessed art thou, O Lord; for a great trance is fallen upon me.
5.6: And he said: Is this indeed the city Jerusalem? I have surely gone astray, for I came by the mountain way; and if my head be heavy and I have not had my fill of sleep, my heart is perplexed within me; and how shall I declare this thing unto Jeremiah, that the city is hidden from me?
5.7: And he sought out all the landmarks that were in the city, to know whether this were Jerusalem. And he went again into the city, and sought if he knew any, and found none. And he said: Blessed art thou, O Lord; for a great trance is fallen upon me. And he went again out of the city afar off, and abode mourning; and whither he would go, he knew not.
5.8: And he set down that basket of figs, and said: I will abide here, until the Lord take this trance from me. And after he had sat, he saw an old man coming from the field. And Abimelech said unto him: Unto thee I speak, thou old man: which is this city? And the old man said unto him: This is Jerusalem.
5.9: And Abimelech said unto him: Where is Jeremiah the priest, and Baruch the Levite, and all the people of this city? for I have found none. And the old man said unto him: Art thou not of this city? and dost thou remember Jeremiah even now, that thou askest concerning him after all this time?
5.10: But Jeremiah is in Babylon with the people; for they were taken captive, and delivered into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Persia; and he went thither to prophesy unto them.
5.11: And when Abimelech heard this from the old man, Abimelech said unto him: If thou wert not an old man, I would laugh thee to scorn; but it is not meet that men should mock an old man; and were it not so, [I would shew thee].
5.12: But as for that thou sayest, that the people were taken captive into Babylon — though the floods of heaven had descended upon them, there hath not been time for them to go into Babylon; and thou sayest the people were taken captive into Babylon!
5.13: And I, as my father Jeremiah sent me, went into the vineyard of Agrippa for a few figs, to give unto the sick that are among the people. I went and came thither, and took that which he commanded me, and returned; and as I went I found a tree, and abode under it to rest, for it was midday; and there I leaned upon the basket of figs, and slept; and I awoke, thinking I had been late, and uncovered this basket of figs, and found them dripping with milk, as when I gathered them, my chosen ones. And thou sayest the people were taken captive into Babylon!
5.14: But behold, see that my figs are not withered. And he uncovered for him the basket of figs, and shewed him; and the old man looked, and lo, the figs were fresh, and their milk dripping.
5.15: Then that old man marvelled, and said unto Abimelech: Thou art righteous, my son; for God would not that thou shouldest see the destruction of the city, and God brought this trance upon thee, and kept thee alive. Behold, it is sixty and six years this day since the people were taken captive into Babylon.
5.16: And if thou wilt know and be sure, my son, look and see in thy field that the crops have not put forth their increase, and that it is not the season for my figs; and know that the time is not the time for all this.
5.17: Then Abimelech cried with a loud voice, saying: I bless thee, O Lord my God; the God of heaven and earth; the rest of the souls of the righteous in all the world.
5.18: And he said unto the old man: What month is this? And he said unto him: The tenth and second of the month Nisan, which is Miyazya. And after this Abimelech gave unto that old man of these figs, and said unto him: God lighten thy way unto the city above, Jerusalem.

6.1: And Abimelech arose, and went forth out of the city, and prayed unto the Lord; and behold, an angel came and led him unto Baruch, and he found him abiding in the tomb.
6.2: And when they knew each other, and had wept between themselves, and kissed one another, he saw the figs in his basket; and he lifted up his eyes unto heaven, and prayed, saying:
6.3: Great is God, who giveth their reward unto his righteous. Rejoice, my soul, and be glad, saying unto the tabernacle of flesh, O holy house; and thy shall be turned into light; and after this the Faithful One cometh, and shall bring thee into thy tabernacle. Abide in thine own virgin faith, and believe, and thou shalt live.
6.4: Behold these figs: lo, sixty and six years since they were gathered, and they are not withered nor rotten, but their milk drippeth until this day. So shall it be done unto thee, my flesh, for thou hast kept thy commandment from the angel of righteousness; who kept the basket of figs, the same shall again keep thee by his power.
6.5: And when Baruch had thus spoken, he turned unto Abimelech and said: Arise, let us pray again, that the Lord may shew us the words which we shall write unto Jeremiah in Babylon, concerning the shelter wherewith he sheltered me.
6.6: And Baruch prayed, and said: My strength, O God, the Lord, and the light that proceedeth out of his mouth: I beseech thee for thy chosen. Great is thy name, and there is none that can know it. Hearken unto the prayer of thy servant, that may be manifest in my heart, thy will to do; and prosper thy priest Jeremiah in Babylon.
6.7: And while he was praying this, an angel came and said unto him: Baruch, minister of light, be not anxious how thou shalt send unto Jeremiah; for at the hour of light an eagle shall come unto thee, and do thou send him concerning Jeremiah; and write in a book, and say unto them thus:
6.8: Unto the children of Israel: as for the stranger that is among you, let him be set apart until fifteen days; and after this I will bring you into the city, saith the Lord.
6.9: He that is not set apart in fifteen [days] from Babylon Jeremiah into the city; and the men of Babylon, saith the Lord.
6.10: And when the angel had said this, he departed from Baruch. And Baruch sent unto the market, and brought papyrus and ink, and wrote, saying:
6.11: By Baruch the servant of God. He writeth a book unto Jeremiah in the captivity of Babylon.
6.12: Rejoice and be glad; for God hath not forsaken us in affliction and desolation; wherefore the Lord remembered us for our tears, and remembered the covenant which he made of old with our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
6.13: And he sent his angel unto me, and told me these words which I send unto thee. These are the words which the Lord, the God of Israel, spake, who brought us out of the land of Egypt: Because ye kept not all his righteousnesses, but lifted up your glory and were haughty before him, he delivered you into the furnace of Babylon, because ye hearkened not unto my word, saith the Lord God, by the mouth of Jeremiah his prophet.
6.14: Them that hear, I will bring out of Babylon; and they shall not be strangers from Jerusalem in Babylon. And if ye will know them and prove them, prove them by the water of Jordan; and he that hearkeneth not shall be by this sign, this which the great seal

7.1: And Baruch arose and went forth from the tomb, and found the eagle sitting without.
7.2: And the eagle said unto him: Hail, Baruch, steward of the faith. And Baruch said unto him: For thou art chosen above all the fowls of heaven, that thou speakest; by the brightness of thine eyes it is manifest; and now shew me what thou doest here.
7.3: And the eagle said unto him: I am sent hither, that thou mayest send by me every word which thou wilt.
7.4: And Baruch said unto him: Canst thou indeed bring this word unto Jeremiah in Babylon? And the eagle said unto him: For this was I sent.
7.5: And Baruch took the book, and fifteen figs from the basket of figs which Abimelech brought, and bound them upon the neck of the eagle.
7.6: And he said: Unto thee I speak, O eagle, king of all birds: go in peace and in safety; carry the message for me; and be not like the raven which Noah sent forth, and it returned not again unto him; but be like the dove which the third time brought word unto Noah. So do thou also take these good words unto Jeremiah, and unto them that are with him, the Israelites, that it may be well with thee; and take this gladness unto the people, the chosen of God.
7.7: And if all the birds surround thee, and all the enemies of righteousness, desiring to kill thee, be strong; and the Lord shall give thee strength. And turn not aside to the right nor to the left, but as a flying arrow go straight; go in the strength of God.
7.8: And when Baruch had said this, the eagle flew with the book, and went into Babylon; and rested upon a post without the city, in a desert place; and abode there until Jeremiah passed by, and some of the people.
7.9: And they passed by there to bury a man that was dead; for Jeremiah had asked Nebuchadnezzar, saying: Give me a place where I may bury [my dead] of my people; and he gave it him.
7.10: And as they went weeping for him that was dead, they came before that eagle; and the eagle cried with a loud voice, saying: Unto thee I speak, Jeremiah, chosen of God: go and gather all the people, and bring them hither, that they may hear the good message which I have brought.
7.11: And when he heard this, he glorified God; and then he gathered all the people, and their wives, and their children, and they came where the eagle was.
7.12: And that eagle came down upon the corpse, and it revived and lived; and this he did that they might believe. And all the people marvelled because of that which was done.
7.13: And they said: Of a truth this is God, who appeared unto our fathers in the wilderness by Moses; and in the likeness of an eagle he appeared unto us, as it were a great eagle.
7.14: And the eagle said unto Jeremiah, saying: Come, loose this book, and read it unto the people; and he read it unto them.
7.15: And when the people heard it, they wept all together, and cast ashes upon their heads; and they said unto Jeremiah: Save us; what shall we do, that we may enter into our city?
7.16: And Jeremiah arose and said unto them: All that ye have heard in the book, so do; and he shall bring you into your city.
7.17: And Jeremiah wrote a book unto Baruch, saying thus: My beloved son, be not weary in prayer, beseeching God for us; that he may lighten our way, until we come out from under the command of this sinful king.
7.18: And thou art found righteous before God, who suffered thee not to come with us, that thou shouldest not see the evil that is done unto them, unto the people in Babylon.
7.19: As a father who hath an only son, and he is delivered up to be punished; and they that are with his father, even they that comfort him, cover their faces, that they may not see the father, who is consumed with grief.
7.20: Even so God had pity on thee, and suffered thee not to come to Babylon, that thou shouldest not see the affliction of the people.
7.21: For since we came into this land, we have had no rest from grief until this day, sixty and six years this day; when we go forth we find of the people some hanged by Nebuchadnezzar the king, weeping and saying: Have mercy upon us, O god of Sor.
7.22: And when I heard this word, I mourned and wept, because the hanged called upon a strange god, saying: Have mercy upon us. And again I remembered the feasts which we kept in Jerusalem, before we were taken captive; and when I remembered, I entered into my house, crying and weeping.
7.23: And now make supplication unto our God, where ye are, thou and Abimelech, for the people, that they may hearken unto my voice and unto the word of my mouth, that they may go out from Persia.
7.24: And now I tell thee: all the time that we have abode here, they have held us, saying: Sing us new songs from the hymns of Zion, the song of your God. And we say unto them: How shall we sing unto you, while we are in a strange land?
7.25: And when Jeremiah had thus written, he bound his book upon the neck of the eagle, and said unto him: Go in peace, and may the Lord keep thee.
7.26: And the eagle went and flew, and brought the book unto Baruch; and Baruch took it and read the book, and wept when he heard of the afflictions of the people and their tribulations.
7.27: And Jeremiah took those figs, and gave them unto the sick that were among the people; and abode teaching them, that they should not do the deeds of the people of Babylon.

8.1: And when the day came wherein God brought the people out of Babylon, and the Lord said unto Jeremiah: Arise, thou and thy people, and come unto Jordan, and say unto the people: Let him that loveth the Lord forsake the works of the people of Babylon.
8.2: And as for the men that took wives from among you, and the women that took [husbands] from them, let us prove them.
8.3: And them that hearken unto thee, bring thou into Jerusalem; but them that hearken not unto thee, suffer them not to enter with thee.
8.4: And Jeremiah thus read unto them all this, and brought them unto Jordan to prove them.
8.5: And as he told them this word which the Lord spake, they that had taken wives murmured, and would not hearken unto Jeremiah; and there were some that said: We will not forsake our wives for ever; we will take them with us into our city.
8.6: And they crossed over Jordan, and came into Jerusalem.
8.7: And Jeremiah and Baruch and Abimelech stood up, saying: Let no man that took [a wife] from Babylon enter into our city.
8.8: And they said unto them that had taken wives for themselves: Arise, let us go into Babylon. And they departed and went.
8.9: And when the men of Babylon saw them, they went forth, that they should not receive them, and suffered them not to enter into Babylon, saying: Ye are our enemies from of old; and secretly ye departed from us. And for this cause ye shall not enter into our city; for we have sworn by the name of our god that ye and your children shall not, for secretly ye departed from us.
8.10: And when they heard this, they returned into Jerusalem, and built for them a town in the districts of Jerusalem; and they called that city Samaria.
8.11: And Jeremiah sent unto them, saying: Repent; and behold, the angel of righteousness shall come, and shall bring you into your place.

9.1: And they abode rejoicing and offering sacrifice seven days for the people.
9.2: And when the tenth day was come, after this was done, Jeremiah offered sacrifice alone.
9.3: And Jeremiah prayed, saying: Holy, holy, holy art thou, the sweet savour unto men, and the light of truth, which enlightenest me until I come before thee.
9.4: I beseech thee for thy people, and I ask thee for the sake of the voice of the seraphim, and for the sake of the sweet savour of the cherubim.
9.5: I ask thee, yea, Michael, the angel of righteousness, who I beseech thee, O Lord of all, and Lord of all, who and didst create all, who and, who didst finish all, and all creation before they were made in secret.
9.6: And when he had prayed this, and finished his prayer, Jeremiah stood up in the temple, and with him Baruch and Abimelech; and Jeremiah became as one whose soul had gone forth from him.
9.7: And then fell Baruch and Abimelech, and cried with a loud voice, saying: Woe unto us, our father Jeremiah, the priest of God, is departed from us.
9.8: And when the people heard this, they ran unto him, and found Jeremiah fallen and dead; and they wept, and rent their garments, and cast ashes upon their heads, and wept with bitter weeping.
9.9: And after they had prepared that wherein they should bury him, there came a voice saying: Bury him not; he is alive, and his soul shall enter into his body again.
9.10: And when they heard this voice, they buried him not; but abode watching him three days, until his soul should enter into his body.
9.11: And there was a voice in the midst of them all, saying: Praise ye with one voice, praise God; and praise ye all the Messiah, the Son of God, who you and you, Jesus, the Son of God, the light of all the world, and the that faileth not, and the life of faith.
9.12: And it shall be after three hundred and three weeks of time for his coming into the land, the tree of life that was in the garden, and was not planted, shall unto every tree that bringeth forth fruit.
9.13: that they may come unto him, and them, that they may bring forth fruit, and; and their fruit shall abide with the angels.
9.14: And for the planting of his tree, that they may and, unto the air, that their roots may not wither, as a plant whose root hath not taken hold of the earth.
9.15: And the red shall ascend as wool; and sweet water shall become bitter, and bitter shall become sweet, with great gladness.
9.16: And the rejoicings of God for the that they may bring forth fruit by the word of his mouth, his Son.
9.17: And he in the night shall enter into the world, and shall choose unto him twelve apostles, that they may see that I have seen which was sent from his Father, who cometh into the world, and upon the mount of Olives he shall and the soul.
9.18: And thus spake Jeremiah concerning the Son of God, that he should come into the world.
9.19: And when the people heard this, they marvelled concerning this, and said: This is the word of Isaiah the son of Amoz, who saith: I have seen God, the Son of God.
9.20: Now arise, let us do unto him as we did unto Isaiah. And they said:; with a stone let us stone him.
9.21: And Baruch and Abimelech cried unto them, saying: With this death ye shall not kill him.
9.22: And Baruch and Abimelech mourned for Jeremiah, and they suffered not the hidden things which he saw.
9.23: And Jeremiah said unto them: weep not; for they cannot kill me, until I make known unto you all that I have seen.
9.24: And now bring ye unto me one stone, and bring ye unto him one stone; and he set it up and said: O light of eternity, this stone, that the likeness of man may be.
9.25: And then the stone became in the likeness of Jeremiah.
9.26: And they took and stoned the stone, supposing it was Jeremiah.
9.27: And Jeremiah made known unto Baruch and Abimelech all the hidden things which he saw; and after he had finished telling them, he went and stood in the midst of the people that he might finish.
9.28: And then that stone cried unto them, saying: O ye lost children of Israel, wherefore do ye stone me, supposing me to be Jeremiah? And Jeremiah, behold, standeth in the midst of you.
9.29: And when they saw, they ran with many stones, and upon him, and buried him; and they took that stone, and placed it in his tomb, and it as a door, and wrote therein, saying: Behold, this is the helper of Jeremiah.
